sanskrit: śrutvā hanūmato vākyaṃ yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ tato 'bravīn mahātejā rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
english: Having heard Hanūmat's words duly and in proper order, the greatly resplendent Rāma, whose valour is true, then spoke.

sanskrit: yāṃ nivedayase laṅkāṃ purīṃ bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ kṣipram enāṃ vadhiṣyāmi satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "That city of Laṅkā belonging to that fearsome rākṣasa, which you describe to me — I shall swiftly destroy it. This I say to you as truth."

sanskrit: asmin muhūrte sugrīva prayāṇam abhirocaye yukto muhūrto vijayaḥ prāpto madhyaṃ divākaraḥ
english: "In this very moment, O Sugrīva, I choose to set out on the march. The hour is auspicious for victory; the sun has reached the meridian."

sanskrit: uttarā phalgunī hy adya śvas tu hastena yokṣyate abhiprayāma sugrīva sarvānīkasamāvṛtāḥ
english: "Today is Uttara-Phālgunī; tomorrow the moon will be joined with Hastā. Let us set forth, O Sugrīva, encompassed by all our army divisions."

sanskrit: nimittāni ca dhanyāni yāni prādurbhavanti me nihatya rāvaṇaṃ sītām ānayiṣyāmi jānakīm
english: "And the auspicious omens that are manifesting before me — slaying Rāvaṇa, I shall bring back Sītā, the daughter of Janaka."

sanskrit: upariṣṭād dhi nayanaṃ sphuramāṇam idaṃ mama vijayaṃ samanuprāptaṃ śaṃsatīva manoratham
english: "Indeed, this upper eye of mine, twitching as it is, seems to herald my victory and the fulfilment of my heart's desire."

sanskrit: agre yātu balasyāsya nīlo mārgam avekṣitum vṛtaḥ śatasahasreṇa vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām
english: "Let Nīla go in advance of this army to reconnoitre the route, attended by a hundred thousand swift monkeys."

sanskrit: phalamūlavatā nīla śītakānanavāriṇā pathā madhumatā cāśu senāṃ senāpate naya
english: "O Nīla, O general, lead the army swiftly by a path furnished with fruits and roots, with cool woodland streams, and abounding in honey."

sanskrit: dūṣayeyur durātmānaḥ pathi mūlaphalodakam rākṣasāḥ parirakṣethās tebhyas tvaṃ nityam udyataḥ
english: "Wicked rākṣasas may defile the roots, fruits, and water along the route; guard against them, remaining ever vigilant."

sanskrit: nimneṣu vanadurgeṣu vaneṣu ca vanaukasaḥ abhiplutyābhipaśyeyuḥ pareṣāṃ nihataṃ balam
english: "Forest-dwellers lurking in ravines, woodland strongholds, and forests might spring forward and scout out the slaughter of our army by the enemy."

sanskrit: sāgaraughanibhaṃ bhīmam agrānīkaṃ mahābalāḥ kapisiṃhā prakarṣantu śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: "Let the mighty lion-monkeys draw forth the fearsome vanguard, which resembles the flood of the ocean, by the hundreds and by the thousands."

sanskrit: gajaś ca girisaṃkāśo gavayaś ca mahābalaḥ gavākṣaś cāgrato yāntu gavāṃ dṛptā ivarṣabhāḥ
english: "Let Gaja, who resembles a mountain, and the great-spirited Gavaya, and Gavākṣa march in front, like lordly bulls at the head of a herd of cattle."

sanskrit: yātu vānaravāhinyā vānaraḥ plavatāṃ patiḥ pālayan dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvam ṛṣabho vānararṣabhaḥ
english: "Let Ṛṣabha, the lord of leaping monkeys, that bull among monkeys, guard the right flank of the monkey host as it advances."

sanskrit: gandhahastīva durdharṣas tarasvī gandhamādanaḥ yātu vānaravāhinyāḥ savyaṃ pārśvam adhiṣṭhitaḥ
english: "Let swift Gandhamādana — fierce as a rutting elephant — take up his post guarding the left flank of the monkey army."

sanskrit: yāsyāmi balamadhye 'haṃ balaugham abhiharṣayan adhiruhya hanūmantam airāvatam iveśvaraḥ
english: "I shall march in the midst of the army, gladdening the flood of warriors, mounted upon Hanūmat as Indra rides upon Airāvata."

sanskrit: aṅgadenaiṣa saṃyātu lakṣmaṇaś cāntakopamaḥ sārvabhaumeṇa bhūteśo draviṇādhipatir yathā
english: "Let Lakṣmaṇa, who equals Death, advance with Aṅgada — as the lord of beings and the lord of wealth ride with the universal sovereign."

sanskrit: jāmbavāṃś ca suṣeṇaś ca vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ ṛkṣarājo mahāsattvaḥ kukṣiṃ rakṣantu te trayaḥ
english: "And let those three — Jāmbavān, Suṣeṇa, and the monkey Vegadarśī, the mighty king of bears — protect the flanks of the army."

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo vāhinīpatiḥ vyādideśa mahāvīryān vānarān vānararṣabhaḥ
english: Having heard the words of Rāghava, Sugrīva, lord of the army and bull among monkeys, assigned posts to the exceedingly valiant monkeys.

sanskrit: te vānaragaṇāḥ sarve samutpatya yuyutsavaḥ guhābhyaḥ śikharebhyaś ca āśu pupluvire tadā
english: Then all those eager-for-battle monkey hosts swiftly leapt up from caves and mountain peaks and bounded forward.

sanskrit: tato vānararājena lakṣmaṇena ca pūjitaḥ jagāma rāmo dharmātmā sasainyo dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Then righteous Rāma, honoured by the monkey king and by Lakṣmaṇa, set forth with his army toward the southern quarter.

sanskrit: śataiḥ śatasahasraiś ca koṭībhir ayutair api vāraṇābhiś ca haribhir yayau parivṛtas tadā
english: He marched then encompassed by monkeys resembling elephants, in their hundreds, their hundreds of thousands, their tens of millions, and their ten thousands.

sanskrit: taṃ yāntam anuyāti sma mahatī harivāhinī
english: The great monkey army followed behind him as he marched.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭāḥ pramuditāḥ sarve sugrīveṇābhipālitāḥ āplavantaḥ plavantaś ca garjantaś ca plavaṃgamāḥ kṣvelanto ninadantaś ca jagmur vai dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Joyful and exultant, all guarded by Sugrīva, the leaping monkeys bounded, leapt, roared, shrieked, and howled as they marched indeed toward the southern quarter.

sanskrit: bhakṣayantaḥ sugandhīni madhūni ca phalāni ca udvahanto mahāvṛkṣān mañjarīpuñjadhāriṇaḥ
english: Eating fragrant honeycombs and fruits, carrying large trees whose blossoms clustered in dense masses,

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ sahasā dṛṣṭā nirvahanti kṣipanti ca patantaś cotpatanty anye pātayanty apare parān
english: suddenly spotting one another they dashed and flung each other about; some fell and others leapt up, and still others knocked their companions to the ground.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo no nihantavyaḥ sarve ca rajanīcarāḥ iti garjanti harayo rāghavasya samīpataḥ
english: "Rāvaṇa must be slain by us, and all the night-roaming rākṣasas too" — thus the monkeys roared in the presence of Rāghava.

sanskrit: purastād ṛṣabho vīro nīlaḥ kumuda eva ca pathānaṃ śodhayanti sma vānarair bahubhiḥ saha
english: In the van, the heroic Ṛṣabha and Nīla and also Kumuda were clearing the route together with many monkeys.

sanskrit: madhye tu rājā sugrīvo rāmo lakṣmaṇa eva ca bahubhir balibhiḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
english: In the centre were King Sugrīva, Rāma, and Lakṣmaṇa — slayers of foes — surrounded by many powerful warriors.

sanskrit: hariḥ śatabalir vīraḥ koṭībhir daśabhir vṛtaḥ sarvām eko hy avaṣṭabhya rarakṣa harivāhinīm
english: The heroic monkey Śatabali, attended by ten crores of soldiers, guarded the entire monkey host single-handedly with his firm grasp.

sanskrit: koṭīśataparīvāraḥ kesarī panaso gajaḥ arkaś cātibalaḥ pārśvam ekaṃ tasyābhirakṣati
english: Kesarī, Panasa, Gaja, and the exceedingly mighty Arka, attended by a hundred crores, guarded one flank of the army.

sanskrit: suṣeṇo jāmbavāṃś caiva ṛkṣair bahubhir āvṛtaḥ sugrīvaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā jaghanaṃ saṃrarakṣatuḥ
english: Suṣeṇa and Jāmbavān, surrounded by many bears, placed Sugrīva in front and together guarded the rear of the army.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ senāpatir vīro nīlo vānarapuṃgavaḥ saṃpatan patatāṃ śreṣṭhas tad balaṃ paryapālayat
english: Their general, heroic Nīla — bull among monkeys, foremost of leapers — guarded that army as it surged forward.

sanskrit: darīmikhaḥ prajaṅghaś ca jambho 'tha rabhasaḥ kapiḥ sarvataś ca yayur vīrās tvarayantaḥ plavaṃgamān
english: Darīmukha, Prajaṅgha, Jambha, and the monkey Rabhasa — those heroes went on every side urging the monkey soldiers onward.

sanskrit: evaṃ te hariśārdūlā gacchanto baladarpitāḥ apaśyaṃs te giriśreṣṭhaṃ sahyaṃ drumalatāyutam
english: Moving thus, those tiger-monkeys, swelling with strength, beheld the foremost of mountains, the Sahya, covered with trees and creepers.

sanskrit: sāgaraughanibhaṃ bhīmaṃ tad vānarabalaṃ mahat niḥsasarpa mahāghoṣaṃ bhīmavega ivārṇavaḥ
english: That great, fearsome monkey army, resembling the flood of the ocean, poured forth with a tremendous roar, like the ocean with its terrifying momentum.

sanskrit: tasya dāśaratheḥ pārśve śūrās te kapikuñjarāḥ tūrṇam āpupluvuḥ sarve sadaśvā iva coditāḥ
english: Those heroic elephant-like monkeys at the side of Daśaratha's son all leapt forward rapidly, like noble steeds urged on.

sanskrit: kapibhyām uhyamānau tau śuśubhate nararṣabhau mahadbhyām iva saṃspṛṣṭau grāhābhyāṃ candrabhāskarau
english: Borne by the two monkeys, those two bulls among men shone gloriously — as though the moon and the sun were touched by two great sea-monsters.

sanskrit: tam aṅgadagato rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhayā girā uvāca pratipūrṇārthaḥ smṛtimān pratibhānavān
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, riding on Aṅgada, addressed Rāma in auspicious words — he who was full of purposeful thought, possessed of memory, and ready of wit.

sanskrit: hṛtām avāpya vaidehīṃ kṣipraṃ hatvā ca rāvaṇam samṛddhārthaḥ samṛddhārthām ayodhyāṃ pratiyāsyasi
english: "Having recovered Vaidehī who was taken, and having slain Rāvaṇa, you shall return with accomplished purpose to Ayodhyā, which likewise waits with accomplished purpose."

sanskrit: mahānti ca nimittāni divi bhūmau ca rāghava śubhānti tava paśyāmi sarvāṇy evārthasiddhaye
english: "O Rāghava, I see great and auspicious omens in the sky and upon the earth — all of them heralding the accomplishment of your purpose."

sanskrit: anu vāti śubho vāyuḥ senāṃ mṛduhitaḥ sukhaḥ pūrṇavalgusvarāś ceme pravadanti mṛgadvijāḥ
english: "An auspicious breeze, gentle and pleasant, blows after the army; and these deer and birds cry out in full, sweet voices."

sanskrit: prasannāś ca diśaḥ sarvā vimalaś ca divākaraḥ uśanā ca prasannārcir anu tvāṃ bhārgavo gataḥ
english: "All the quarters are serene; the sun shines clear and unclouded; and Venus — of brilliant, cloudless flame — follows behind you."

sanskrit: brahmarāśir viśuddhaś ca śuddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ arciṣmantaḥ prakāśante dhruvaṃ sarve pradakṣiṇam
english: "The cluster of Brahmā shines pure; the great seers shine pure and radiant; all of them blaze forth steadily in the auspicious rightward direction."

sanskrit: triśaṅkur vimalo bhāti rājarṣiḥ sapurohitaḥ pitāmahavaro 'smākam iṣkvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām
english: "Triśaṅku the royal sage, together with his priest, shines without blemish — that most excellent ancestral star of our great-souled Ikṣvākus."

sanskrit: vimale ca prakāśete viśākhe nirupadrave nakṣatraṃ param asmākam ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām
english: "Viśākhā also shines bright and undimmed, without affliction — that supreme constellation of our great-souled Ikṣvāku line."

sanskrit: nairṛtaṃ nairṛtānāṃ ca nakṣatram abhipīḍyate mūlaṃ mūlavatā spṛṣṭaṃ dhūpyate dhūmaketunā
english: "The constellation of the rākṣasas, Nairṛta, is tormented; Mūla, their own natal star, is afflicted and scorched by a comet with a smoky tail."

sanskrit: saraṃ caitad vināśāya rākṣasānām upasthitam kāle kālagṛhītānāṃ nakatraṃ grahapīḍitam
english: "This portends the destruction of the rākṣasas — whose time has come, seized by Death — their star tormented by a planet."

sanskrit: prasannāḥ surasāś cāpo vanāni phalavanti ca pravānty abhyadhikaṃ gandhā yathartukusumā drumāḥ
english: "The divine waters are pure and the rivers are serene; the forests are fruit-laden; fragrances waft most abundantly; trees bloom as in their proper season."

sanskrit: vyūḍhāni kapisainyāni prakāśante 'dhikaṃ prabho devānām iva sainyāni saṃgrāme tārakāmaye
english: "The arrayed monkey armies blaze brilliantly, O master, like the armies of the gods in the war against Tārakā."

sanskrit: evam ārya samīkṣyaitān prīto bhavitum arhasi iti bhrātaram āśvāsya hṛṣṭaḥ saumitrir abravīt
english: "Having observed all these omens, O noble one, you ought to be joyful." Thus Saumitri, himself elated, spoke these words to reassure his brother.

sanskrit: athāvṛtya mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ jagāma mahatī camūḥ ṛkṣavānaraśārdūlair nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhair vṛtā
english: Then the great host, covering the entire earth, marched onward — accompanied by tiger-bears and tiger-monkeys, armed with claws and fangs.

sanskrit: karāgraiś caraṇāgraiś ca vānarair uddhataṃ rajaḥ bhaumam antardadhe lokaṃ nivārya savituḥ prabhām
english: The dust raised by the tips of the monkeys' hands and feet swallowed the earth, blocking the sun's radiance and enshrouding the world.

sanskrit: sā sma yāti divārātraṃ mahatī harivāhinī hṛṣṭapramuditā senā sugrīveṇābhirakṣitā
english: That great monkey army marched day and night — a force joyful and exultant, guarded by Sugrīva.

sanskrit: vanarās tvaritaṃ yānti sarve yuddhābhinandanaḥ mumokṣayiṣavaḥ sītāṃ muhūrtaṃ kvāpi nāsata
english: All the monkeys pressed forward swiftly, rejoicing in battle, eager to free Sītā — not halting anywhere even for a moment.

sanskrit: tataḥ pādapasaṃbādhaṃ nānāmṛgasamākulam sahyaparvatam āsedur malayaṃ ca mahī dharam
english: Then they reached the Sahya mountain, thick with trees and teeming with diverse animals, and also the great earth-bearing Malaya.

sanskrit: kānanāni vicitrāṇi nadīprasravaṇāni ca paśyann api yayau rāmaḥ sahyasya malayasya ca
english: Even while beholding the variegated forests and the river-springs of Sahya and of Malaya, Rāma pressed on.

sanskrit: campakāṃs tilakāṃś cūtān aśokān sinduvārakān karavīrāṃś ca timiśān bhañjanti sma plavaṃgamāḥ
english: The leaping monkeys broke campaka trees, tilaka trees, mango trees, aśoka trees, sinduvāra trees, karavīra trees, and timiśa trees.

sanskrit: phalāny amṛtagandhīni mūlāni kusumāni ca bubhujur vānarās tatra pādapānāṃ balotkaṭāḥ
english: The powerful monkeys there consumed fruits with the fragrance of ambrosia, roots, and blossoms of the trees.

sanskrit: droṇamātrapramāṇāni lambamānāni vānarāḥ yayuḥ pibanto hṛṣṭās te madhūni madhupiṅgalāḥ
english: Those tawny-brown monkeys, joyful and of a golden hue, marched on drinking honeycombs the size of a droṇa measure that hung pendant from the branches.

sanskrit: pādapān avabhañjanto vikarṣantas tathā latāḥ vidhamanto girivarān prayayuḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: The bull-monkeys pressed forward, breaking trees, tearing down creepers, and toppling mountain-boulders.

sanskrit: vṛkṣebhyo 'nye tu kapayo nardanto madhudarpitāḥ anye vṛkṣān prapadyante prapatanty api cāpare
english: Other monkeys roared in the trees, drunk with honey; others ran to the trees and still others fell from them.

sanskrit: babhūva vasudhā tais tu saṃpūrṇā haripuṃgavaiḥ yathā kamalakedāraiḥ pakvair iva vasuṃdharā
english: The earth was filled by those bull-monkeys — like the earth covered with fields of fully bloomed lotuses.

sanskrit: mahendram atha saṃprāpya rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ adhyārohan mahābāhuḥ śikharaṃ drumabhūṣitam
english: Then reaching Mount Mahendra, lotus-eyed Rāma, long-armed, ascended the summit adorned with trees.

sanskrit: tataḥ śikharam āruhya rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ kūrmamīnasamākīrṇam apaśyat salilāśayam
english: Having climbed the summit, Rāma the son of Daśaratha beheld the expanse of waters teeming with tortoises and fish.

sanskrit: te sahyaṃ samatikramya malayaṃ ca mahāgirim āsedur ānupūrvyeṇa samudraṃ bhīmaniḥsvanam
english: Passing beyond the Sahya and the great mountain Malaya, they reached in due course the ocean, roaring with a terrifying sound.

sanskrit: avaruhya jagāmāśu velāvanam anuttamam rāmo ramayatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sasugrīvaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Rāma — foremost among those who bring delight — descended swiftly and came with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa to the incomparable shore-forest.

sanskrit: atha dhautopalatalāṃ toyaughaiḥ sahasotthitaiḥ velām āsādya vipulāṃ rāmo vacanam abravīt
english: Then, having reached the broad shoreline — its rocky surface washed by the sudden surges of water — Rāma spoke these words.

sanskrit: ete vayam anuprāptāḥ sugrīva varuṇālayam ihedānīṃ vicintā sā yā na pūrvaṃ samutthitā
english: "We have now reached, O Sugrīva, the abode of Varuṇa. Here now arises that anxiety which did not arise before."

sanskrit: ataḥ paramatīro 'yaṃ sāgaraḥ saritāṃ pati na cāyam anupāyena śakyas taritum arṇavaḥ
english: "Yonder is the far shore — this ocean, lord of rivers. And this sea cannot be crossed without a means."

sanskrit: tad ihaiva niveśo 'stu mantraḥ prastūyatām iha yathedaṃ vānarabalaṃ paraṃ pāram avāpnuyāt
english: "Therefore let the encampment be made here and let counsel be taken here — such that this monkey army may reach the far shore."

sanskrit: itīva sa mahābāhuḥ sītāharaṇakarśitaḥ rāmaḥ sāgaram āsādya vāsam ājñāpayat tadā
english: Speaking thus, long-armed Rāma — worn by grief over Sītā's abduction — upon reaching the ocean ordered the camp to be established.

sanskrit: saṃprāpto mantrakālo naḥ sāgarasyeha laṅghane svāṃ svāṃ senāṃ samutsṛjya mā ca kaś cit kuto vrajet gacchantu vānarāḥ śūrā jñeyaṃ channaṃ bhayaṃ ca naḥ
english: "The time for counsel has arrived for us regarding the crossing of this ocean. Let each corps be dismissed to its own position; let no one stray in any direction. Let the heroic monkeys go and reconnoitre; the hidden dangers facing us must be known."

sanskrit: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīvaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ senāṃ nyaveśayat tīre sāgarasya drumāyute
english: Having heard the words of Rāma, Sugrīva together with Lakṣmaṇa encamped the army on the tree-covered shore of the ocean.

sanskrit: virarāja samīpasthaṃ sāgarasya tu tad balam madhupāṇḍujalaḥ śrīmān dvitīya iva sāgaraḥ
english: That army, encamped near the ocean, blazed in splendour — like a second ocean, its waters pale gold as honey.

sanskrit: velāvanam upāgamya tatas te haripuṃgavāḥ viniviṣṭāḥ paraṃ pāraṃ kāṅkṣamāṇā mahodadheḥ
english: Then those bull-monkeys, having come to the shore-forest, settled down there, yearning for the far shore of the great deep.

sanskrit: sā mahārṇavam āsādya hṛṣṭā vānaravāhinī vāyuvegasamādhūtaṃ paśyamānā mahārṇavam
english: That monkey army, having reached the great ocean and joyful, gazed upon the great ocean tossed by the force of the wind.

sanskrit: dūrapāram asaṃbādhaṃ rakṣogaṇaniṣevitam paśyanto varuṇāvāsaṃ niṣedur hariyūthapāḥ
english: Gazing upon the abode of Varuṇa — its far shore distant, its expanse unobstructed, haunted by hosts of rākṣasas — the monkey troop-leaders sat down.

sanskrit: caṇḍanakragrahaṃ ghoraṃ kṣapādau divasakṣaye candrodaye samādhūtaṃ praticandrasamākulam
english: Fearsome with its violent crocodiles and sea-monsters, churned at the close of day and at moonrise, roiling with moon-halos,

sanskrit: caṇḍānilamahāgrāhaiḥ kīrṇaṃ timitimiṃgilaiḥ dīptabhogair ivākrīrṇaṃ bhujaṃgair varuṇālayam
english: scattered with monstrous sea-beasts lashed by fierce winds, strewn with timitimiṅgila creatures — the abode of Varuṇa seemed blanketed with serpents of blazing coils.

sanskrit: avagāḍhaṃ mahāsattair nānāśailasamākulam durgaṃ drugam amārgaṃ tam agādham asurālayam
english: Plunged into by great creatures, filled with many underwater mountains, difficult to ford, treacherous, pathless, fathomless — that dwelling of the asuras.

sanskrit: makarair nāgabhogaiḥ ca vigāḍhā vātalohitāḥ utpetuś ca nipetuś ca pravṛddhā jalarāśayaḥ
english: Churned by makara sea-dragons and serpent coils, reddened by the wind — great masses of water rose up and fell down.

sanskrit: agnicūrṇam ivāviddhaṃ bhāskarāmbumanoragam surāriviṣayaṃ ghoraṃ pātālaviṣamaṃ sadā
english: As if scattered with fire-powder, dazzling with the sun's reflections — the charming realm of the sun's enemy, fearsome, forever rendered rough by the underworld.

sanskrit: sāgaraṃ cāmbaraprakhyam ambaraṃ sāgaropamam sāgaraṃ cāmbaraṃ ceti nirviśeṣam adṛśyata
english: The ocean appeared like the sky and the sky appeared like the ocean — ocean and sky appeared indistinguishable from one another.

sanskrit: saṃpṛktaṃ nabhasā hy ambhaḥ saṃpṛktaṃ ca nabho 'mbhasā tādṛgrūpe sma dṛśyete tārā ratnasamākule
english: The waters were merged with the sky and the sky was merged with the waters; in that aspect they appeared alike — the stars mingled with the jewels.

sanskrit: samutpatitameghasya vīcci mālākulasya ca viśeṣo na dvayor āsīt sāgarasyāmbarasya ca
english: Between the ocean with its billowing clouds and its rows of wave-garlands and the sky, no distinction could be made.

sanskrit: anyonyair āhatāḥ saktāḥ sasvanur bhīmaniḥsvanāḥ ūrmayaḥ sindhurājasya mahābherya ivāhave
english: The waves of the ocean-king, crashing against one another and intertwined, rang out with terrifying sounds — like great war-drums in battle.

sanskrit: ratnaughajalasaṃnādaṃ viṣaktam iva vāyunā utpatantam iva kruddhaṃ yādogaṇasamākulam
english: Resounding with the rush of jewel-strewn waters, as if lashed by the wind, as if leaping in rage, teeming with hosts of sea-creatures,

sanskrit: dadṛśus te mahātmāno vātāhatajalāśayam aniloddhūtam ākāśe pravalgatam ivormibhiḥ bhrāntormijalasaṃnādaṃ pralolam iva sāgaram
english: those great-souled heroes beheld the water-abode battered by the wind, as if hurled into the sky by the wind, as if bounding up with its waves — the ocean seemingly churning with the roar of its swirling, wave-tossed waters.

sanskrit: sā tu nīlena vidhivat svārakṣā susamāhitā sāgarasyottare tīre sādhu senā niveśitā
english: Then that army, with its proper guard duly arranged by Nīla, was well encamped on the northern shore of the ocean.

sanskrit: maindaś ca dvividhaś cobhau tatra vānarapuṃgavau viceratuś ca tāṃ senāṃ rakṣārthaṃ sarvato diśam
english: And both Mainda and Dvivida — those two bull-monkeys — roamed in every direction around that army for its protection.

sanskrit: niviṣṭāyāṃ tu senāyāṃ tīre nadanadīpateḥ pārśvasthaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmo vacanam abravīt
english: When the army had encamped on the shore of the lord of rivers and lakes, Rāma, seeing Lakṣmaṇa at his side, spoke these words.

sanskrit: śokaś ca kila kālena gacchatā hy apagacchati mama cāpaśyataḥ kāntām ahany ahani vardhate
english: "They say that grief passes away with the passage of time; but mine, as I do not see my beloved, grows greater day by day."

sanskrit: na me duḥkhaṃ priyā dūre na me duḥkhaṃ hṛteti ca etad evānuśocāmi vayo 'syā hy ativartate
english: "It is not that my beloved is far — that does not grieve me. It is not that she was taken — that does not grieve me. This alone is what I lament: her youth is passing away."

sanskrit: vāhi vāta yataḥ kanyā tāṃ spṛṣṭvā mām api spṛśa tvayi me gātrasaṃsparśaś candre dṛṣṭisamāgamaḥ
english: "Blow, O wind, from wherever that maiden is — touching her, touch me also. Through you I have contact with her body; through the moon I have a meeting of eyes."

sanskrit: tan me dahati gātrāṇi viṣaṃ pītam ivāśaye hā nātheti priyā sā māṃ hriyamāṇā yad abravīt
english: "That burns my limbs like poison swallowed and lodged within me — what my beloved cried to me as she was being carried off: 'O my lord!'"

sanskrit: tadviyogendhanavatā taccintāvipulārciṣā rātriṃ divaṃ śarīraṃ me dahyate madanāgninā
english: "Fed by that separation as by fuel, blazing with great flames of thought of her, by night and by day my body is consumed by the fire of love."

sanskrit: avagāhyārṇavaṃ svapsye saumitre bhavatā vinā kathaṃ cit prajvalan kāmaḥ samāsuptaṃ jale dahet
english: "I shall plunge into the ocean and sleep, O Saumitri, apart from you; perhaps the blazing passion might burn me even as I lie submerged in the water."

sanskrit: bahv etat kāmayānasya śakyam etena jīvitum yad ahaṃ sā ca vāmorur ekāṃ dharaṇim āśritau
english: "There is much to sustain life for one who still desires — by this alone: that I and she of beautiful thighs are supported by one and the same earth."

sanskrit: kedārasyeva kedāraḥ sodakasya nirūdakaḥ upasnehena jīvāmi jīvantīṃ yac chṛṇomi tām
english: "As a dry field lives by the moisture of the irrigated field beside it, so I live by the mere proximity of her vitality — for I hear that she is alive."

sanskrit: kadā tu khalu susśoṇīṃ śatapatrāyatekṣaṇām vijitya śatrūn drakṣyāmi sītāṃ sphītām iva śriyam
english: "When indeed shall I see fair-hipped Sītā — her eyes as wide as lotus petals — radiant as Śrī, after vanquishing my enemies?"

sanskrit: kadā nu cārubimbauṣṭhaṃ tasyāḥ padmam ivānanam īṣadunnamya pāsyāmi rasāyanam ivāturaḥ
english: "When shall I, like a sick man drinking an elixir, drink from her face which is like a lotus, lifting it gently upward — from those beautiful lips red as the bimba fruit?"

sanskrit: tau tasyāḥ saṃhatau pīnau stanau tālaphalopamau kadā nu khalu sotkampau hasantyā māṃ bhajiṣyataḥ
english: "When indeed shall those two firm, full breasts of hers — resembling the fruits of the tāla palm — trembling, embrace me as she laughs?"

sanskrit: sā nūnam asitāpāṅgī rakṣomadhyagatā satī mannāthā nāthahīneva trātāraṃ nādhigacchati
english: "She — that dark-eyed one with the long eyes, virtuous though surrounded by rākṣasas, who calls me her lord — no doubt finds no protector, as though she were lordless."

sanskrit: kadā vikṣobhya rakṣāṃsi sā vidhūyotpatiṣyati vidhūya jaladān nīlāñ śaśilekhā śaratsv iva
english: "When shall she, shaking off the rākṣasas and rising up free of them, soar aloft — as the crescent moon in autumn shakes free of blue storm-clouds?"

sanskrit: svabhāvatanukā nūnaṃ śokenānaśanena ca bhūyas tanutarā sītā deśakālaviparyayāt
english: "Sītā, naturally slender, is surely grown yet more slender still through grief and fasting — and by the reversal of her rightful place and season."

sanskrit: kadā nu rākṣasendrasya nidhāyorasi sāyakān sītāṃ pratyāhariṣyāmi śokam utsṛjya mānasaṃ
english: "When indeed shall I, having fixed my arrows in the breast of the rākṣasa king, bring Sītā back and cast off this grief from my mind?"

sanskrit: kadā nu khalu māṃ sādhvī sītāmarasutopamā sotkaṇṭhā kaṇṭham ālambya mokṣyaty ānandajaṃ jalam
english: "When indeed shall chaste Sītā — resembling the daughter of the immortals, filled with longing — cling to my neck and shed tears born of joy?"

sanskrit: kadā śokam imaṃ ghoraṃ maithilī viprayogajam sahasā vipramokṣyāmi vāsaḥ śukletaraṃ yathā
english: "When shall I suddenly shed this dreadful grief born of separation from the Maithilī — as one sheds a white garment that has turned otherwise?"

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapatas tasya tatra rāmasya dhīmataḥ dinakṣayān mandavapur bhāskaro 'stam upāgamat
english: While wise Rāma lamented thus at that place, the sun, his body dimming at the end of the day, descended to the west.

sanskrit: āśvāsito lakṣmaṇena rāmaḥ saṃdhyām upāsata smaran kamalapatrākṣīṃ sītāṃ śokākulīkṛtaḥ
english: Comforted by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma performed the evening rites — remembering Sītā of lotus-petal eyes, overwhelmed by grief.

sanskrit: laṅkāyāṃ tu kṛtaṃ karma ghoraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhavāvaham rākṣasendro hanumatā śakreṇeva mahātmanā abravīd rākṣasān sarvān hriyā kiṃ cid avāṅmukhaḥ
english: In Laṅkā, having witnessed the fearsome, life-threatening deed wrought by Hanūmat — as by great-souled Śakra himself — the rākṣasa king, his face turned slightly downward in shame, addressed all his rākṣasas.

sanskrit: dharṣitā ca praviṣṭā ca laṅkā duṣprasahā purī tena vānaramātreṇa dṛṣṭā sītā ca jānakī
english: "Laṅkā, this city so difficult to assail, has been violated and penetrated — by a mere monkey, at that — and Sītā, daughter of Janaka, was seen."

sanskrit: prasādo dharṣitaś caityaḥ pravarā rākṣasā hatāḥ āvilā ca purī laṅkā sarvā hanumatā kṛtā
english: "The pleasure-grove was ravaged, the sacred shrine was violated, eminent rākṣasas were slain, and all of Laṅkā was thrown into turmoil — all by Hanūmat."

sanskrit: kiṃ kariṣyāmi bhadraṃ vaḥ kiṃ vā yuktam anantaram ucyatāṃ naḥ samarthaṃ yat kṛtaṃ ca sukṛtaṃ bhavet
english: "What shall I do? May good befall you all. What is the right course to follow now? Tell me what is fitting — let that be done which, having been done, will prove well done."

sanskrit: mantramūlaṃ hi vijayaṃ prāhur āryā manasvinaḥ tasmād vai rocaye mantraṃ rāmaṃ prati mahābalāḥ
english: "The noble and wise declare that victory has counsel as its root; therefore I choose indeed to take counsel, O mighty ones, regarding Rāma."

sanskrit: trividhāḥ puruṣā loke uttamādhamamadhyamāḥ teṣāṃ tu samavetānāṃ guṇadoṣaṃ vadāmy aham
english: "Men in the world are of three kinds — the highest, the lowest, and the middling; of these gathered together I shall speak of their virtues and defects."

sanskrit: mantribhir hitasaṃyuktaiḥ samarthair mantranirṇaye mitrair vāpi samānārthair bāndhavair api vā hitaiḥ
english: "He who, together with counsellors who are well-disposed and capable in resolving deliberations — or with friends of equal purpose, or even with well-wishing kinsmen —"

sanskrit: sahito mantrayitvā yaḥ karmārambhān pravartayet daive ca kurute yatnaṃ tam āhuḥ puruṣottamam
english: "— deliberates and then sets forth his undertakings, and also makes effort in what pertains to fate — him they call the highest of men."

sanskrit: eko 'rthaṃ vimṛśed eko dharme prakurute manaḥ ekaḥ kāryāṇi kurute tam āhur madhyamaṃ naram
english: "He who deliberates alone on matters of interest, alone sets his mind on dharma, and alone performs his tasks — him they call the middling man."

sanskrit: guṇadoṣāv aniścitya tyaktvā daivavyapāśrayam kariṣyāmīti yaḥ kāryam upekṣet sa narādhamaḥ
english: "He who, without determining the merits and defects, abandoning recourse to the divine, neglects his task with the word 'I shall act' — he is the lowest of men."

sanskrit: yatheme puruṣā nityam uttamādhamamadhyamāḥ evaṃ mantro 'pi vijñeyo uttamādhamamadhyamaḥ
english: "Just as men are forever of three kinds — highest, lowest, and middling — so too counsel itself must be understood to be highest, lowest, and middling."

sanskrit: aikamatyam upāgamya śāstradṛṣṭena cakṣuṣā mantriṇo yatra nirastās tam āhur mantram uttamam
english: "Counsel wherein the counsellors, having arrived at unity by means of the eye of śāstra, come to a settled conclusion — that they call the highest counsel."

sanskrit: bahvyo 'pi matayo gatvā mantriṇo hy arthanirṇaye punar yatraikatāṃ prāptaḥ sa mantro madhyamaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: "Counsel wherein the counsellors, even after many opinions have been advanced in determining what is beneficial, yet again arrive at a single conclusion — that is remembered as middling counsel."

sanskrit: anyonyamatim āsthāya yatra saṃpratibhāṣyate na caikamatye śreyo 'sti mantraḥ so 'dhama ucyate
english: "Counsel wherein each upholds his own opinion and speaks against the others, where there is no good outcome in any unity of view — that counsel is called the lowest."

sanskrit: tasmāt sumantritaṃ sādhu bhavanto mantrisattamāḥ kāryaṃ saṃpratipadyantām etat kṛtyatamaṃ mama
english: "Therefore, O foremost of counsellors, let you all well deliberate and agree upon what should be done — this is the most urgent matter for me."

sanskrit: vānarāṇāṃ hi vīrāṇāṃ sahasraiḥ parivāritaḥ rāmo 'bhyeti purīṃ laṅkām asmākam uparodhakaḥ
english: "Rāma, surrounded by thousands of heroic monkeys, is advancing upon our city of Laṅkā — he who would lay siege to us."

sanskrit: tariṣyati ca suvyaktaṃ rāghavaḥ sāgaraṃ sukham tarasā yuktarūpeṇa sānujaḥ sabalānugaḥ
english: "And Rāghava shall most certainly cross the ocean with ease — with fitting swiftness, together with his brother and followed by his army."

sanskrit: asminn evaṃgate kārye viruddhe vānaraiḥ saha hitaṃ pure ca sainye ca sarvaṃ saṃmantryatāṃ mama
english: "With affairs having reached this pass — opposed by the monkeys — let everything beneficial for the city and for the army be deliberated thoroughly on my behalf."
